evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Character Database), CUHK
evidence.text: The database gives a tentative reading of an oracle-bone form as 坐. For Warring States forms it analyzes 卩 over 土 as a person kneeling on the ground; it describes Qin forms as doubled 卩, later graphically corrupted so that Shuowen interpreted the upper part as 畱省. It attributes the proposal connecting 坐 and 危 to Chen Jian. These are source-reported analyses, not direct verification here of the excavated forms.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: Shuowen Jiezi, as quoted by CUHK Chinese Character Database
evidence.text: The entry quotes Shuowen as glossing 坐 止也 and citing 土 and 畱省. In the CUHK account, this is a Han-period analysis following the reported corruption of the Qin form; it is not independent proof of the earlier graphic structure.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.text: The entry associates the kneeling-sitting sense with examples from Zuozhuan and Liji; it separately cites seat/place (Han Feizi, Shiji), keeping watch (Zuozhuan and a Mawangdui manuscript), criminal implication (Shiji, Hanshu), legal confrontation (Zuozhuan), and causal use (Yuefu poetry and a Tang poem). These are cited textual examples, not dates of surviving witnesses or a demonstrated order of semantic change.

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The dictionary records multiple historical graphic variants of 坐 and cites Shuowen's analysis, Han clerical inscriptions, and later lexicographic sources. It describes the modern standard 坐 as the regular-script form of the ancient graph, and some variants as graphic transformations; this supports graphic diversity but does not establish a single direct evolution for all forms.

evidence.text: The entry lists examples for sitting, travel by vehicle, staying or guarding, seat/place, legal senses, and causal use. Examples include texts named Liji, Zuozhuan, Lunyu, Shiji, and Hanshu. The page does not date manuscript witnesses, so it supports reported textual attestations rather than a secure chronology among senses.

gaps: The Shang oracle-bone identification as 坐 remains tentative in the inspected CUHK account; no primary inscription image or excavation publication was independently checked.

The dossier's simple two-people-on-earth account is not independently confirmed by the inspected paleographic account. The competing 卩 + 土 analysis and proposed corruption path are source-reported scholarly analyses, not directly demonstrated here from primary artifact images.
The proposed relationship between 坐 and 危 remains attributed to Chen Jian and is not established as settled.

Classical source titles and quotations are reported attestations; surviving witness dates and a secure relative chronology of individual senses were not established. In particular, the semantic derivations behind travel-by-vehicle and causal ‘because’ remain unproven here.
No whole-graph loan or phonetic component was proposed in the inspected sources. No component readings are applicable; only 坐's supplied local current and Baxter–Sagart readings are recorded.

The Commons image is an explicitly modern digital reconstruction in seal style, not an artifact photograph. Its exact pixels could not be inspected because the original URL returned HTTP 429; select it only as a candidate for visual-agent review.
The Xiaoxuetang page did not expose character-specific records in the browser output, so no image or rights claim for a selected glyph is included.

No tracked extract is recommended: the inspected Commons lead is a single image with adequate character-specific provenance and an explicit page-level permission statement; no recurring corpus requiring extraction was established.
